subject: Mac OS X Rstan 2.2 broken with g++? clang++ seems to be fine.

messages.author: 0839befa8a8b7d53
messages.subject: Mac OS X Rstan 2.2 broken with g++? clang++ seems to be fine.
parts:
I know people have been seeing this compile problem with RStan 2.2 (and began with RStan 2.1.1) on some Macs. Several of my students have been experiencing this issue, which is how it came to my attention. The pattern is that RStan compiles fine, but when compiling a model, it throws a messy error that begins with

Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) : 
  Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created!

It goes on for a while. I'll attach a full example as a text file. (Top of file has the relevant g++ -v output.)

I finally had a chance to sit down and try to isolate the issue. I think the problem is isolated to g++ 4.2.x, as I have been able to fix it by using clang++ to build Rstan, both under 10.7.x and 10.8.x (I dare not install 10.9, as everyone says it's evil).

So provided one has clang installed, all that's needed to fix the problem is to edit ~/.R/Makevars to include:

CXX = clang++

Then remove RStan and recompile. 

If this does indeed fix it for everyone, then maybe not worth fixing, as clang is available for everyone. But it is definitely worth putting a big flashing signal on RStan wiki about it, so everyone adds CXX=clang++ to their Makevars.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Mac OS X Rstan 2.2 broken with g++? clang++ seems to be fine.
parts:
It is a known issue with Rcpp that will probably be fixed soon, so I haven't spent much time trying to work around it on the rstan side. Even if it weren't broken, I can't imagine why someone would actively want to use the (llvm-)g++ 4.2.x that comes with Xcode, even though it is the default used by R on Macs. It is basically just the llvm frontend with a 2007 version of the g++ library, which isn't tested much by Boost or Eigen or Stan. If I had a Mac, I would just use llvm / clang / libc++. My mostly Mac-using students are going to be installing RStan soon, and I am not planning to deal with (llvm-)g++ 4.2.x at all.

Ben
